cards.q: Match each property with what it means.
pairs: The load per area it takes before yielding or breaking
How well it resists dents and scratches
How much energy it absorbs before it fractures
How far it stretches before it breaks
cards.why: A file is hard but not tough; mild steel is tough and ductile but not very hard.

cards.q: A test bar of {a} mm² breaks at a peak load of {f} kN. What is its tensile strength, in MPa?
cards.why: Tensile strength = peak load ÷ original area; N/mm² is MPa.

cards.q: Which test measures toughness?
cards.why: Charpy swings a pendulum through a notched bar and measures the energy absorbed. Brinell and Vickers measure hardness.

cards.q: What does more carbon do to a plain carbon steel?
options: Harder and stronger, but less weldable
Softer, and easier to bend and form
Rust-proof, much like a stainless steel
cards.why: Mild steel (about 0.2% C) welds and bends easily; high-carbon steels harden for tools but crack more readily when welded.

cards.q: What makes stainless steel resist rust?
options: A zinc coating on the surface
Chromium, which forms an oxide film
cards.why: The chromium oxide film re-forms when scratched, as long as oxygen reaches it. Some stainless grades are magnetic.

cards.q: A {m} kg steel bracket is remade the same size in aluminium. Steel is 7.85 g/cm³ and aluminium 2.7 g/cm³. What does the new one weigh, in kg?
cards.why: Same volume, so mass scales with density: about a third. It is also about a third as stiff, so it may need to be thicker.

cards.q: A medium-carbon steel is heated red hot, then quenched in water. What happens?
cards.why: Rapid cooling traps the carbon in a hard, brittle structure (martensite). Tempering then trades some hardness for toughness.

cards.q: Why is hardened steel tempered?
cards.why: Reheating to a lower temperature relieves the brittleness of the quenched structure. Higher tempering temperatures give tougher, softer steel.

cards.q: What does annealing do?
options: Coats it with a layer of zinc
cards.why: Heating and cooling slowly gives a soft, ductile structure, easy to machine or form. Case hardening is what hardens only the surface.

cards.q: What is CFRP?
options: Carbon steel with a plastic coat
Carbon fibres held in a resin
cards.why: Carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer: strong, stiff fibres bonded by a resin matrix that holds them and passes load between them.

cards.q: Why are plies laid at a mix of angles, such as 0°, ±45° and 90°?
options: It makes the finished part look even
Resin shrinks less when laid at 45°
Fibres are only strong along their length
It uses up the offcuts of cloth
cards.why: A laminate is designed like a structure: the layup puts fibres along the load paths.

cards.q: Which defect is typical of composites and found by ultrasonic testing?
cards.why: Impact, poor cure or voids can separate plies; porosity and disbonds too. They lie parallel to the surface, so UT finds them well.

cards.q: Stainless steel bolts hold an aluminium panel outdoors. Which metal corrodes at the joint?
cards.why: In a wet joint the less noble metal (aluminium) becomes the anode and corrodes. Insulating washers or sealant break the circuit.

cards.q: How does galvanising protect steel?
options: It turns the steel into stainless steel
It is a paint that dries very hard
It hardens the steel's surface layer
It seals the steel and corrodes in its place
cards.why: Zinc is less noble than steel, so it corrodes sacrificially where the coating is damaged.

cards.q: Two metals form a galvanic couple and only one is to be painted. Which, and why?
cards.why: Painting the anode leaves any defect as a tiny anode driven by a huge cathode: fast, deep pitting.

cards.q: Match each welding process with its description.
pairs: Wire fed through the torch, with a shielding gas
Tungsten electrode, separate filler, very controllable
Automatic, under a blanket of granular flux
cards.why: They differ in how the arc is shielded and how filler is added.

cards.q: Which weld defects are usually the most serious?
cards.why: Planar flaws have sharp edges that grow under load and fatigue. Small, rounded porosity is usually less harmful.

cards.q: An arc runs at {v} V and {i} A, travelling at {s} mm/min, with a thermal efficiency of 0.8. What is the heat input, in kJ/mm?
cards.why: Heat input = efficiency × V × I × 60 ÷ (1000 × travel speed in mm/min).

cards.q: Match each G-code with what it does.
pairs: Straight-line move at the feed rate
cards.why: The core motion codes in ISO 6983 G-code.

cards.q: The cutting speed should be {vc} m/min. The workpiece is {d} mm in diameter. What spindle speed is that, in rpm?
cards.why: $n = \frac{1000 V_c}{\pi D}$: the surface must travel $V_c$ metres a minute, and each turn moves it $\pi D$ mm.

cards.q: A {z}-flute cutter runs at {n} rpm with a feed of {fz} mm per tooth. What table feed is that, in mm/min?
cards.why: Feed rate = rpm × teeth × feed per tooth.

cards.q: How does FDM (fused deposition) printing work?
options: It lays melted plastic down in layers
It fuses metal powder with a laser
It cures liquid resin with light
It cuts sheets and glues them up
cards.why: Cheap and common for jigs, fixtures and prototypes.

cards.q: When is additive manufacturing a good choice?
cards.why: It needs no tooling, so it wins on low volumes and complex geometry; machining or moulding win on volume.

cards.q: Why is an FDM part usually weakest in one direction?
options: The printer runs slower that way
Layers bond less well than each bead
The nozzle cools one side only
cards.why: Loads that pull layers apart (across the build direction) break it soonest: orient the part so the load runs along the layers.

cards.q: A company is certified to ISO 9001. What does that certify?
cards.why: It covers how the organisation plans, controls, records and improves its work, audited by a certification body.

cards.q: A dimension's tolerance band is {t} mm wide. The process's standard deviation is {s} mm. What is Cp?
cards.why: $C_p = \frac{USL - LSL}{6\sigma}$: the tolerance against the process spread. 1.33 or more is a common target.

cards.q: A shaft is 20 ± {t} mm. The process mean is {mu} mm and its standard deviation {s} mm. What is Cpk?
cards.why: $C_{pk} = \frac{\min(USL - \mu, \mu - LSL)}{3\sigma}$: like Cp, but it penalises a mean that is off centre.
